chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Shādhān ibn al-Khalīl, from Yūnus, from Yaḥyā ibn Ṭalḥah, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sulaymān, who said:
I heard Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام saying: “Wudu (ablution) after ghusl (ritual bath) is an innovation.”

So the proper understanding of this report is what we mentioned in the first report: that if he believes that the ghusl does not suffice for him, then he would be introducing an innovation. It is also possible that the report is specific to other than ghusl al-janābah, because among the sunnah (prophetic tradition) in these ritual baths is that wudu (ablution) be done in them before them; so if he delays it until after the ghusl, he would be introducing an innovation.

key_terms.الْمَسْنُونِ: that which is established as sunnah (prophetic tradition)
key_terms.الْوُضُوءُ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing before salat (prayer)
key_terms.غُسْلَ الْجَنَابَةِ: the ghusl performed for the state of janābah

ai.seo_question: Is performing wudu after ghusl considered bid'ah in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This report states that performing wudu (ablution) after ghusl (ritual bath) is bid'ah (innovation). The accompanying explanation clarifies that this applies when one believes ghusl is insufficient by itself, or in cases other than ghusl al-janābah where the sunnah is to perform wudu before the ghusl rather than after it.
